title: Transitivity of separable field extensions
statement: Let $k\subseteq K\subseteq L$ be a tower of fields [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose $K/k$ and $L/K$ are separable in the possibly transcendental sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: every intermediate field finitely generated as a field over the base is separably generated over it. Then $L/k$ is separable in the same sense. No finiteness, algebraicity or perfectness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness) and Tag 030W (lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions): in characteristic $p$, $L\otimes_kk^{1/p}=L\otimes_K(K\otimes_kk^{1/p})$ is reduced; characteristic zero is automatic. Agent combination of the two lemmas; reviewer-added node (Q70 maintainer review).

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable] directly to $L/k$. Otherwise write $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$; $p$ is prime since $k$ is a field. Fix an arbitrary field extension $E/k$. We shall prove that $L\otimes_k E$ is reduced, with tensor rings carrying the multiplication of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property].

source.place: Tag 00TX, lemma-characteristic-zero-local-smooth, first sentence of proof; Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, condition (4).

proof.text: Put $R=K\otimes_k E$. For a nilpotent $x\in R$, write $x=\sum_{i=1}^r a_i\otimes e_i$ using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and set $K_0=k(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\subseteq K$. By the assumed separability of $K/k$ and [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], $K_0/k$ is separably generated. Since the field $E$ is reduced, [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] makes $K_0\otimes_k E$ reduced. Its canonical map to $R$ is injective: $E$ is a flat $k$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], so [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] applies to $K_0\hookrightarrow K$ after swapping the tensor factors. The swap and its inverse send $u\otimes v$ to $v\otimes u$ and are well-defined by bilinearity. The map is a ring map by the pure-tensor multiplication. The lift $x_0=\sum_i a_i\otimes e_i$ therefore satisfies $x_0^n=0$ whenever $x^n=0$, $n>0$, by injectivity. Reducedness gives $x_0=0$, hence $x=0$. Thus $R$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, finitely generated reduction in the separable case; Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, (4) implies (1).

proof.text: Next put $T=L\otimes_K R$, regarding $R$ as a $K$-algebra through $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. For a nilpotent $y\in T$, write $y=\sum_{j=1}^s b_j\otimes r_j$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and set $L_0=K(b_1,\ldots,b_s)\subseteq L$. The assumed separability of $L/K$ and [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] make $L_0/K$ separably generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] over the field $K$ to $L_0$ and the reduced $K$-algebra $R$ of step 2. It gives reducedness of $L_0\otimes_K R$; it does not require $R$ to be a field. The $K$-vector space $R$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], so [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] applied to $L_0\hookrightarrow L$ and the bilinear tensor swap makes $L_0\otimes_K R\to T$ injective. For the lift $y_0=\sum_j b_j\otimes r_j$, the ring-map identity and injectivity give $y_0^n=0$ from $y^n=0$. Hence $y_0=0$ and $y=0$. Thus $T$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 030U, lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, finitely generated reduction in the separable case; Tag 030W, lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions, (4) implies (1).

proof.text: The tensor universal properties [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give inverse ring maps $\Phi:L\otimes_K(K\otimes_k E)\to L\otimes_k E$ and $\Psi:L\otimes_k E\to L\otimes_K(K\otimes_k E)$ with $\Phi(b\otimes(a\otimes e))=ba\otimes e$ and $\Psi(b\otimes e)=b\otimes(1\otimes e)$. The formulas respect additivity and balancing over $k$ and $K$: in particular $bc\otimes(a\otimes e)$ and $b\otimes(ca\otimes e)$ have the same image for $c\in K$. They preserve products and units by the pure-tensor formula. Their composites fix $b\otimes e$ and $b\otimes(a\otimes e)$, the latter because $ba\otimes(1\otimes e)=b\otimes(a\otimes e)$ by $K$-balancing. Pure tensors generate, so the composites are identities. A nilpotent $z\in L\otimes_k E$ has nilpotent image $\Psi(z)$, zero by step 3; applying $\Phi$ gives $z=0$.

source.place: Tags 030U and 030W, tensor-reassociation assembly; maps and inverses written out from the tensor universal property.

proof.text: Since $E/k$ was arbitrary, step 4 proves reducedness of $L\otimes_k E$ for every extension field $E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-reduced-extension-separable] to $L/k$ and the prime $p$ of step 1. Its only additional hypothesis is precisely this reducedness for every $E/k$. Its conclusion is that every finitely generated intermediate field of $L/k$ is separably generated, which is the required separability. Neither tower extension was assumed finite, algebraic, finitely generated or over a perfect field.

proof_origin.place: Agent assembly of Tag 030U (finite-tensor reduction, twice) and Tag 030W ((4) implies (1)); characteristic zero by Tag 00TX. Tensor reassociation checked on generators.
